en: He enriched the people for whom he was an eye
In the lineage of this stock
A man with two hundred coats
He raided peoples and caused ruin
This kinsman suffered from deceit
He was the man who struck down both
He cast tumult across this world
This fighter followed a ruinous road
Old Kuspur took one
He made that one into a people
Your son himself was absent
The raiders trampled out a road
Dwelling along the river valleys
Where passing men made homes
A thousand spears went to the mountain
What a man descended from Tobokel
From what lineage was his blood
Black-mace Oroybek
That old Oroybek accepted the faith
Lord Kurguk took his daughter
He crushed and destroyed them
Dear Kozoy was a khan
He brought all of them low
Ebedey and Kozoy, two giants
Coming with a great host to fight
Turning, saying, here is the black one
Ebedey and Kozoy set out
They went into hardship
Those men drove on in vain
There was no success
May no dark day fall upon your head
A road gathered toward paradise
Hearing the taunting words to the people
Tumult rose from where you camped
His hardening wrath was strong
What you saw had not existed
Saying that, abandon hope in life
Taking eighty champion companions
A hero remained with Olbu
Those who remained said, enter by oath
They pierced and made a path
His hooked nose was like a shield
Driving the red-necked one
Like a mountain set down
The orphan heir guarding the land
Among beasts that wielded bows
A hero who caught mankind’s eye
Struck down like spring lightning
Enduring this, he took companions
Chyngyr Kozoy burned with grief
Turning back without faltering
He turned away from his wrath
The hero prepared to mount
He turned toward the multitude
Ebedey and Kozoy, two lions
Holding their spears
The hero Seytek upon his horse
Clashing beneath white caps
Roaring like great wolves
Among his kin and men
Asking what to do among the people
Suffering thundered around them
Putting on their armor and swords
A red-mottled black shaft
Prepared to contend from then on
The young men went forth at sunrise
A thousand under the hero’s shadow went out
Driving the devil’s daughter by the muzzle
The pale one Keltet
The demon-devil led them astray
Meeting the spirit-blessed warrior
Keltet mounted his horse
They cried out before Khan Chynka
Those who grappled remained
The enemy pressed toward Talas
Keltet cut the road
Raising a sacred standard
Keltet launched the attack
Of Ebedey and Kozoy, the two
The Chinese enemy against the Kyrgyz
Keltet attacked
With his moon-bright sword
He comes saying he will take revenge
The red-marked one goes under the moon
Let him rejoice when the host meets
The thousands who saw the fierce one
The daughter of the khan of Kashgar
May she calm the courageous one
He says, I will cast your name from the palace
Janaly and Karak, two men
Saying, I will take a spoonful of his blood
Taking no counsel from the troubled place
Taking no arrow from the field
Saying, let the men die
They stood tall and advanced
Looking toward the steep ground
Ebedey and Kozoy, two men
Great Kongdu fastened his load
Crossing the pass toward the city
Now forced to sustain them
They raced them back across the plain
Countless men flashed their swords
They watched and joined battle
Taking round measures of grain
Taking nine animals for slaughter
Eating the finest colt of the herd
Consuming nine portions of rich fat
They pursued for two days
Settlements like gardens
As though his elder Karak had died
He seized it with great force
Lying upon every mountain
Thousands clashed in calamity
They received the enemy’s fire
They fell upon the road
There was a pacer
They drove hard along the road
They stunned those on the road
They raced like horses off the path
The two had the same fate
They occupied the broken ridge
The third was called a people welded together
Facing them, his spirit flared
A dagger was tied at his waist
Teeth gleamed right and left
There was mystery in his mottled frame
Kozoy who drove the horse
He had a form mysterious beyond the world
You are heroes; have no fear
The hero had a cauldron-dark gaze
He had harsh words to speak
His dark eyes were like pits
Spoken words carry weight
When the contest came to Seytek
He had a need to fight
Anger struck his face like stone
Hurrying fiercely toward safety
Saying, why should he come to Talas
Two hundred were arrayed
From the ridge toward the Kyrgyz
Saying, I will stage the contest
The words spoken to the hero became news
They rush forward in alarm
The two lambs gather into a group
Looking, his eyes widened
Of one faith, like true believers
Appearing all together without leaving one behind
Hero Seytek took his turn
The hero pressed on in distress
If this Kozoy were left alone
He looked ready to sacrifice his life
Blood came from Ebedey and Kozoy
Their lives ebbed from their courage
The leopards grappled
Saying this battle will pass
Grit your teeth and reach the fight
When the proud one was engaged
Those who met crossed blades
The two giants, exhausted
Were left amid the child’s tumult
They acted like great demons
Each lusting to defeat the other
They drove each other like beasts
They cast their backs toward death
Ak Joltoy amid the circle
Hero Seytek was to trip him
He devastated the gathered host
Then Ak Bermet
Met them and turned back
Driving on from Kumurska,
Forgetting even God’s thousands,
Taking road after road,
Crossing a mountain with a high ridge,
Fording the Karakuurai River,
His appearance striking the multitude,
Roaring ferociously,
The ground trembling where he stepped,
The boldest of the heroes,
Meeting one another separately,
Setting out freely upon the road,
Travelling onward fiercely,
Wearied by travelling afar,
From before the one called Armane,
Pursuing his father’s might,
Girding himself as he climbed the pass,
Swaying this way at full length,
Showing that he was a grey-maned champion,
Putting on solid iron armor,
After much time had passed, taking up a spear,
The cities of Kokon and Andijan,
Thinking of mounting up and taking the road,
The man he would meet was Er Seitek,
His escort roaring fiercely,
Driving them on ahead,
Wisdom and resourcefulness are true arts,
What weapons did those Kalmyks have,
Loading it upon him at a comfortable place,
Never tiring at the horse’s mane,
Training horses and drilling the troops,
Between him and his master Köböy,
The child who would remain between them,
The Kalmyks spared not a single one,
They would seize them while sweeping through the ravine,
Countless calamities befell Sal-Kashka,
If he wandered, it was another calamity,
Kashka had many ranks of warriors,
Holding shields and thundering,
Straining forward, drawing water at the waist,
Lashing the head with oil,
All of the heroes,
Spurred their horses and took the road,
These two Kalmyks.
He regarded these thousands as equals,
Lengthening his stirrup-stride,
Redd­ening his eyes like a storm cloud,
Not forgetting the hero’s condition,
Er Emes came downhill,
No less than a hero’s son,
In anger, his courage was hard as stone,
Tall Koykok, broad of stature,
Kök-Kashka was ready to strike,
His valor was of another order,
Following the riverbed, they travelled on,
What he intended was a single encounter,
Ride wide through the affairs of the age,
The old man who would remain among them,
His dusty countenance was apparent,
Spending the night in a comfortable place,
If someone dismantled his grey yurt,
Only in the firm place at Rushkuta,
Naming a time for their battle,
Hoping for the brave one,
Making it strike the rope evenly,
Without turning back to look,
If you hear his melody, it is sorrowful,
Thundering toward the autumn heights,
Not grieving for its blue expanse,
Taking clear aim at [?],
Outside, calamity and misfortune,
When they encountered it, they became agitated,
The heroes of the Elei-Kotai people,
Their bodies bristling at [?],
Mocking one another,
Coming into this place,
A quarrel arose from what was said,
Coming into the house,
Man against man,
The foolish one who thinks he knows much,
Vying through his greatness,
May he not abandon reason at all,
Taking the side of the living host,
His game of overturning,
He leaves [?] awakened,
Becoming a true spectacle himself,
Never retreating from anything,
Becoming water that overflowed and spread,
